cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: How Much Do You Know?
cards.instruction: Probe for what others know while revealing as little as possible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll straighten out this party story. Tell me exactly what you've heard before it gets any bigger.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The cake went over the balcony. But I'm not naming who told me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No names needed. We can keep this informal. Did you hear a description, or actually see what happened?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's supposed to be a video. I haven't watched it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we're working from the same report then. Keep your source to yourself; just tell me whether anyone has described what's visible in the video.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims control of story; A3 grants anonymity to keep B talking; A5 preserves that condition while probing whether video contents have been described, revealing no A actions.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 source refusal; A5 uses B4 unwatched video to separate direct viewing from descriptions.

relationship.evidence: B2 protects source and B4 gives limited evidence within that boundary, plausible cooperative informant.

heightening.evidence: A5 narrows B4 evidence without demanding the name A agreed not to require.

specificity.evidence: A1 party/cake incident and B4 supposed video give clear stakes; no inconsistent brother disclosure remains.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 same report is a face-saving alignment with B rather than new factual explanation.
